courses.name: Italian Game: Giuoco Piano
courses.intro: The classical way to play 1.e4 e5: quick development, pressure on f7 and a big pawn centre with c3 and d4.

line.note: Take the centre and open lines for the queen and bishop.
Develop with a threat: the knight attacks e5.
The bishop aims at f7, the weakest point near Black's king.
Preparing d4 to build a strong pawn centre.
Strike in the centre now that d4 is supported.
Recapture with a pawn and keep two big centre pawns.
Block the check while developing a piece.
Recapture towards the centre. White has more space; Black hits back with ...d5.
Black challenges the centre at once. This is the main line of the Giuoco Piano.

courses.name: Italian Game: Quiet Plan (d3)
courses.intro: A calm, modern way to play the Italian: protect e4 with d3, castle, and prepare d4 later.

line.note: A solid move that defends e4 and avoids sharp tactics.
King safety first.
The rook supports e4 and prepares a later d4 break.
Gives the bishop a retreat to c2 and prepares d4. A typical slow-build setup.

courses.name: London System
courses.intro: A system you can play against almost anything: d4, Bf4, e3, Nf3, c3, Nbd2 and Bd3.

line.note: Develop the dark-squared bishop before playing e3, so it is not shut in.
Solid pawn chain; the bishop on f4 stays active.
The c3, d4, e3 triangle makes the centre hard to break.
Keep the good bishop: retreat rather than allowing ...Bxf4.
All pieces developed. Next comes castling, then play for e4 or a kingside attack.

courses.name: Queen's Gambit Declined (as White)
courses.intro: Classical central play: pressure on d5, a pin with Bg5, and slow, strategic manoeuvring.

line.note: The Queen's Gambit: offer a wing pawn to remove Black's centre pawn.
Add pressure on d5.
Pin the knight that defends d5.
Solid development; the f1 bishop can now come out.
Keep the pin.
The Tartakower setup: Black prepares ...Bb7 to fight for the light squares.

courses.name: 1...e5 against the Italian (as Black)
courses.intro: Meet 1.e4 with 1...e5 and develop naturally: a great way to learn open positions.

line.note: Take your share of the centre.
Defend e5 while developing.
Mirror White: the bishop aims at f2.
Develop with an attack on e4.
Support e5 and open the c8 bishop's diagonal.
Castled and fully developed. A healthy, balanced position.

courses.name: Caro-Kann: Classical
courses.intro: A solid answer to 1.e4: support ...d5 with ...c6 and develop the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain.

line.note: Prepare ...d5 with pawn support.
Challenge the centre immediately.
The key Caro-Kann idea: the bishop gets out before ...e6.
Keep the bishop on the long diagonal.
Give the bishop a safe square on h7.
Prepare ...Ngf6 without allowing doubled pawns.
The bishop is safe on h7. Black is solid and will finish with ...Ngf6 and ...e6.

courses.name: Caro-Kann: Advance Variation
courses.intro: When White pushes e5, develop the bishop first, then attack the d4 pawn with ...c5.

line.note: Develop the bishop before closing it in with ...e6.
Solid: now the f8 bishop can develop.
Hit the base of White's pawn chain.
Develop and add pressure; Black often follows with ...Ne7 and ...Nc6.

courses.name: French Defence: Advance
courses.intro: After 3.e5, attack the base of White's pawn chain on d4 with ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Qb6.

line.note: Prepare ...d5 with a solid pawn.
Challenge e4.
Attack the d4 pawn: the base of White's chain.
More pressure on d4.
The queen joins the attack on d4 and b2.
Gain queenside space and stop White's b4 ideas.

courses.name: Sicilian Najdorf: English Attack
courses.intro: The most famous Sicilian. Black fights for d5 and plays on the queenside, while White often castles long and attacks.

line.note: Unbalance the game from move one.
Trade a wing pawn for White's centre pawn.
The Najdorf move: controls b5 and prepares ...e5 or ...b5.
Gain space and chase the knight.
Fight for the key d5 square.
White prepares Qd2, long castling and g4. Sharp play ahead.

courses.name: Queen's Gambit Declined (as Black)
courses.intro: Hold the d5 point firmly, develop calmly, and free your game later with ...c5 or ...e5.

line.note: Claim the centre.
Decline the gambit and keep a strong pawn on d5.
Break the pin by developing.
King safety first.
Support a later ...c5 or ...e5 break.
Rock-solid. Black is ready for ...dxc4 and ...Nd5 to free the position.

courses.name: Slav Defence
courses.intro: Defend d5 with the c-pawn and keep the light-squared bishop free.

line.note: Support d5 without blocking the c8 bishop.
Take the pawn now that White can't easily win it back with b4.
The bishop develops outside the pawn chain.
Open the f8 bishop.
Pin the knight and fight for e4. A classical main line.

courses.name: King's Indian Defence: Classical
courses.intro: Let White take the centre, then strike back with ...e5 and attack on the kingside.

line.note: Prepare to fianchetto the bishop.
The bishop on g7 will be Black's best piece.
Control e5 before striking.
Castle quickly.
The key counter-strike in the centre.
Add pressure on d4.
The knight heads for the kingside, ready for ...Nd7 and ...f5.
